text:
dmitri: quick heads-up — ran a targeted perf sweep for small-seq workloads across L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. hitting weird tail spikes when KV cache is warm and batching is enabled. numbers below, looking for hypotheses and a short-term prescript.

perf-bot: summary from sweep (seq<=64, model: redwood-small, batch target 8, kv-warm after 100 requests)
```
device  | kernel            | median(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms)
L4      | fmha_fast_small   | 18         | 55      | 220
T4      | fmha_fast_small   | 20         | 60      | 240
A10     | fmha_fast_small   | 12         | 28      | 45
A100    | nvfuser_fused     | 8          | 14      | 25
H100    | nvfuser_fused     | 6          | 12      | 20
```
Observations: p99 on L4/T4 is dominated by intermittent 150–300ms spikes after KV cache warms; flamegraphs point at `kv_prefetch()` -> kernel selection fallback path -> memcopy on host.

alice: that pattern smells like a bad codepath when KV cache is in-use + batching merges requests that change seq_len distribution. iirc we have a runtime fallback that switches kernels if an expected kernel fails or OOMs — could be thrash between two kernels and extra memcpy.

ben: can you paste the microprofile for the hot request? also whether batching heuristic did cross-batch coalescing (we sometimes merge variable seqs into a single kernel call)

dmitri: microprofile (trimmed):
```
request 12345: enqueue 0.5ms -> batch_coalesce 2.1ms -> select_kernel 0.2ms -> launch(fmha_fast_small) 1.3ms -> kv_prefetch 3.4ms -> memcpy(host->dev) 180ms -> kernel_retry(nvfuser_fallback) 2.0ms -> success
```
Note: memcpy duration only showed up on L4/T4 runs. A10/A100/H100 did not hit that memcpy cost.

carla: memcpy that big on L4/T4 could be because of a pinned/unpinned buffer mismatch or crossing PCIe vs NVLink path. L4/T4 in shared nodes use PCIe only; A100/H100 might be using NVLink/FBP so memmove cheaper.

dmitri: good point. but why only after KV warm? hypothesis: KV cache uses a staging buffer on host when entries exceed some page size, we then try to upload on-demand. On faster devices with bigger BAR or NVLink it's fine; on PCIe devices the on-demand upload stalls and triggers kernel fallback.

ben: two short-term mitigations:
- bump `kv_upload_threshold` so we upload larger chunks asynchronously during idle, avoid on-request host->dev memcpy.
- change batching heuristic: don't coalesce variable lengths into same kernel on PCIe devices (prefer per-request small-launch rather than coalescing causing a heavyweight memcpy).

alice: long-term we should add device-aware kernel presets and an autotune probe at model load. proposal:
- seq buckets: 1-32, 33-64, 65-256
- device families: pciedev (L4/T4), ampere-mid (A10), ampere-hpc (A100/H100)
- map kernels: pciedev+1-32 -> fmha_small_prefetch (avoid host staging), pciedev+33-64 -> fmha_small_locked, ampere-hpc -> nvfuser_fused
- autotune job: run 50 synthetic requests across bucket combos at model load (cheap, <1s) and persist best kernel in model config

carla: +1. Also add a runtime safeguard: if we detect >3 host memcpy stalls in 1s for a model on a device, flip to fallback kernel that avoids host staging and mark an alert in console.

infra-bot: noted — created ticket INF-4312: "Device-aware kernel presets + KV hotpath safeguards" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

dmitri: implemented quick patch to bump kv_upload_threshold to 512KB and disable cross-seq coalescing on PCIe in an A/B config. running a short retest now.

perf-bot: retest numbers (same config, after patch):
```
L4 | fmha_fast_small (no-coalesce) | median 20ms | p95 30ms | p99 48ms
T4 | fmha_fast_small (no-coalesce) | median 22ms | p95 34ms | p99 52ms
```
So p99 improved massively (from 220ms -> ~50ms). median slightly up but acceptable.

ben: nice. next steps to land:
- formalize seq->kernel presets in runtime config schema
- implement quick autotune probe (only for new model versions or after infra changes)
- add runtime memcpy-stall detector and automatic fallback with metadata tag

alice: I'll draft the runtime config layout and a minimal autotune PR. carla, dmitri can you help validate on A10/L4 clusters? aim to ship a v1 preset in next sprint.

carla: will run validation tomorrow on L4 fleet and report back.

dmitri: thanks all — saved us from noisy p99 regressions. tagging @product for visibility :eyes:
